data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet summarizes performance and equity-related patterns for Montenegro using PISA 2022 assessment results for 15-year-old students. It reports trends in mathematics, reading, and science compared with earlier PISA cycles (notably 2018 and 2015) and describes the distribution of performance using proficiency levels (e.g., Level 2 as a baseline and Levels 5–6 as top performance). The factsheet also highlights within-country gaps by socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles and top vs bottom quarters), gender differences (similar mathematics performance but higher reading for girls), and immigrant background patterns (differences not significant after accounting for socio-economic profile). It further reports contextual indicators from student, school, and principal questionnaires (belonging, life satisfaction, classroom discipline, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning experiences), while noting that the COVID-related section is based on a reduced response rate (74%) in Montenegro. No student-level predictive modeling or ML methods are evaluated in this document; it is a descriptive reporting of OECD’s published PISA 2022 database tables.
